item.title: Poland: Footage shows people taking cover as a gunman opens fire in Krakow
item.description: Footage shows people fleeing as cars speed away during a deadly shooting at Krakow's Main Market Square, which left six people dead and about 15 injured.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure
item.description: Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.

item.title: Liverpool FC targets counterfeit pro-Palestinian shirts using altered club crest
item.description: On the internet, fake Premier League shirts with pro-Palestinian slogans are on sale, affecting, among other clubs, Liverpool F.C. The Reds are now taking action.

item.title: Video shows people fleeing as gunman opens fire in Kraków, Poland
item.description: UGC footage shows people running for cover as a deadly shooting unfolds in Kraków, Poland, leaving at least six people dead and around a dozen wounded, according to police.

item.title: 'Peace is possible and we are called to build it' Pope Leo XIV says in Uruguay
item.description: The Pontiff was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. Leo's sixth apostolic journey comes less than a month after lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.

item.title: ‘We need to change everything’: Mélenchon uses Le Bourget rally to press home his programme
item.description: The right to vote at 16, a Sixth Republic as a “new ecological state”: the four-time Élysée candidate outlined his presidential programme to more than 20,000 supporters. A further show of strength against a backdrop of social unrest in the country.

item.title: Six killed and more than a dozen injured after gunman opens fire in historic centre of Kraków
item.description: The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical" and “ultra-nationalistic" views, Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said.

item.title: Russia fires North Korean missiles at 'key' Ukrainian energy facility, Zelenskyy says
item.description: "Moscow is deliberately seeking to leave millions of Ukrainians without electricity, heating, and water as winter approaches," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said.

item.title: Spain: Baby's body found in freezer in Ourense may have been there over 20 years
item.description: The body of the newborn was discovered in a chest freezer in a storage room in Allariz (Ourense) and may have been there for over 20 years, according to local newspaper 'La Región'.

item.title: Cyberattacks target Italian foreign minister and company behind Brenner Base Tunnel project
item.description: The company behind the under-construction Brenner Base Tunnel project - a 55 km rail link between Innsbruck in Austria and Fortezza in Italy - confirmed it had also been hit by a cyberattack in recent weeks.

item.title: US launches new targeted strikes on Iran as Trump claims progress in talks with Tehran
item.description: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems, sending ripples across the Gulf, but Trump insists they are “minor strikes” while intense diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all-out war.

item.title: US offers $20 million reward and 'possible relocation' for information on 'Iran’s nuclear program'
item.description: The State Department said: "The regime’s lack of compliance with the IAEA on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of 'continuity of knowledge.'"

item.title: Pedro Alliana sworn in as Paraguay president after Santiago Peña's impeachment
item.description: Ousted ex-President Santiago Peña was placed under house arrest on Friday after he was impeached over a major banking crisis.

item.title: US Secret Service arrests man parked near White House with 'multiple guns' in vehicle
item.description: The suspect has been charged with multiple offences, including possession of dangerous weapons and theft, per the DHS. He is in the custody of the US Marshals Service.

item.title: New Zealand counts votes in razor-thin election after campaign centred on cost of living
item.description: In New Zealand, people cast a party vote as well as an electorate vote in a general election. With their electorate vote, New Zealanders vote for a candidate to represent their local electorate in parliament. They also vote for the party they want to be in government.

item.title: Hackers probed Europe’s fridge systems weeks before cyberattacks. Who did it and what could they target next?
item.description: The attacks exposed basic security weaknesses in connected refrigeration systems, but experts warn that similar vulnerabilities could put everything from supermarket equipment to hospital and data centre infrastructure at risk.

item.title: When antibiotics stop working: Europe's growing superbug threat
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance, responsible for an estimated 35,000 deaths each year in the European Union, is spreading across humans, animals and the environment, prompting calls for a broader approach to tackling one of public health's biggest challenges.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv region injure at least six and damage bridge and energy facilities
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on Friday night of further strikes against Ukraine's energy sector and civilian infrastructure as he renewed calls for deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles.

item.title: Europe needs Cold War-like deterrence for AI warfare, Poland says
item.description: The rise in AI-powered cyberattacks requires Europe to build a deterrence system similar to the one that prevented mutual destruction during the Cold War, Polish Deputy Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski has said.

item.title: ‘Brief burst of intense heat’ could give hard-to-recycle wind turbine blades a second life
item.description: Europe risks becoming a dumping ground for hard-to-recycle wind turbine blades but new research has found a ‘hot’ solution

item.title: Earn points, save cash: A basic guide to frequent-flyer programmes in Europe
item.description: With airline alliances and partnerships, frequent flyers can rack up miles in their sleep.

item.title: 'We have proven ourselves': UAE vows to remain reliable energy supplier to Europe
item.description: One of the UAE's most senior energy officials told Euronews diversification has carried the country's energy sector through months of regional crisis, as Europe looks to the Gulf for secure supply.

item.title: Are Europeans saving enough for retirement? Here is how much more they need to put aside
item.description: To retire on 70% of their pay, workers on average wages could need to save more than €1,000 extra a month in Switzerland and more than €600 in Germany. Euronews Business compares the estimates for women and men across Europe.

item.title: Polar vortex weakens weeks ahead of schedule, raising risk of cold spells
item.description: Meteorologists warn that an unprecedented early disruption of the polar vortex could increase the risk of cold spells across the Northern Hemisphere, although its impact on the coming winter remains uncertain.

item.title: From gastronomy to sports: What to discover in Spain's Region of Valencia
item.description: It will be a big year for the Spanish region in 2027, with major events including SailGP and the MotoGP Valencia Grand Prix on the calendar.

item.title: A trip to the Philippines offers hidden gems, slow food and colourful events
item.description: Beyond its capital Manila, the Philippines offers travellers a menu of slow food, coastal activities and festivals not to miss.

item.title: Starring Great Britain: How set-jetting is helping distribute tourists across the regions
item.description: VisitBritain is encouraging people to set off and explore the stunning scenery captured on film and TV.

item.title: US measles cases exceed 5,000 in 2026, reaching their highest level in 35 years
item.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 measles cases so far this year, the highest annual figure in 35 years, according to official data released on Friday.

item.title: Foreign buyers push Spanish home sales to record 16% amid record prices
item.description: The property market has reached record highs in prices and foreign purchases (16.05%), while sales and mortgages have fallen for a third straight quarter, signalling a slowdown in activity.

item.title: Nearly 1,000 migrants rescued from seven boats off El Hierro in Spain
item.description: Around 700 of the rescued migrants are due to be transferred to Tenerife to relieve pressure on reception facilities, while several people required hospital treatment.

item.title: Trump appoints immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
item.description: Miller, one of the driving forces behind US president Donald Trump's mass deportation policy, is set to succeed Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff next week.

item.title: EU rejects Trump’s 'big beautiful' security deal with Russia and 'all of Europe'
item.description: European leaders push back against Washington’s proposal for a broader security framework, warning that Moscow cannot dictate the continent’s future as US-led peace negotiations over Ukraine prepare to resume in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: France's Mélenchon to stage major campaign rally for manifesto launch
item.description: The leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, is currently polling second ahead of next spring's presidential elections, according to a poll conducted in late October.

item.title: Switzerland: Giant banner targets Big Tech outside data centre site
item.description: Greenpeace activists unfurled a giant 26-by-26-metre banner outside a data centre construction site in Beringen, northeastern Switzerland, on Friday 6 November, protesting against the growing environmental impact of major technology companies.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Elon Musk's Tesla to 'wind down' Cybertruck production next year
item.description: Musk said the decision was taken in order to make room for increased production of its Cybercab robotaxi. The move comes after years of weaker-than-expected sales for the futuristic electric pickup.

item.title: Spain: Vintage cars hit the streets of Almería for annual rally
item.description: Around 40 vintage and classic cars have taken to the streets of Almería for the 36th edition of an annual rally. From a rare 1905 Vermorel to a DeLorean, the event celebrates more than a century of motoring history.

item.title: ‘We vote with our money’: What are the biggest commercial opportunities of EU enlargement?
item.description: “The European market is the best market in the world,” says investment expert Jan Růžička, urging policymakers to accelerate EU accession and the Capital Markets Union to maintain momentum and sustain enthusiasm among candidate countries.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father arrested over child sex abuse images
item.description: Markle Sr's arrest follows an investigation launched after his son, Thomas Markle Jr, reportedly discovered boxes containing hundreds or potentially thousands of images at his father's former home in the Philippines.

item.title: Iran delivers secret Khamenei message to Putin as Moscow pushes gas pipeline deal
item.description: Iran’s Security Council chief, Mohsen Rezaei, went to Moscow to deliver a personal message from Ayatollah Khamenei and discuss building a pipeline to import Russian gas.

item.title: Singapore Airlines to invest €1.4 billion upgrading luxury long-haul cabins
item.description: Updates include the largest double bed in commercial aviation in first class, pyjamas for business class passengers and Bluetooth pairing with the in-flight entertainment system.

item.title: Baku real estate expo showcases Azerbaijan’s tech-driven urban future
item.description: What makes a city attractive to investors and the people who live there? From affordable housing and urban planning to smart technologies and changing lifestyles, Azerbaijan’s first International Real Estate Exhibition put the future of the built environment in focus.

item.title: Tiny Spanish island quits coal for good amid renewables boom — but country struggling to electrify
item.description: Authorisation has been granted to permanently close down the remaining coal-fired units on Majorca, marking a new era for the island.

item.title: Group of lawyers suing French interior minister over protesters' life-changing injuries
item.description: Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during recent demonstrations in France say they will take legal acton against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

item.title: From street eats to Michelin stars: Why foodies should visit Macao in 2027
item.description: It’s a big year for Macao in 2027 as it celebrates 10 years of being a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy. Travellers are invited to explore its fusion food scene as well as its ‘quieter’ spots.

item.title: Kazakhstan’s growth to pick up in 2027 despite geopolitical tensions, IMF says
item.description: The IMF expects Kazakhstan’s economy to grow by 4.9% in 2027, up from 4.4% this year. Kazakhstan is forecast to grow faster than any other oil exporter in the IMF’s Middle East and Central Asia group in 2026.

item.title: Data centre backlash: Which AI companies have been affected by US midterm results?
item.description: OpenAI has gone on a charm offensive, while semiconductor companies worldwide have seen their stocks plunge.
